title: Universal platform delivery fabric productization plan
purpose: Define the owned Rust, cloud-native, API-driven, productized pipeline/control-plane direction that supersedes CLI-shaped, shell-shaped, vendor-authority, and oya-/cloud-prefixed destination assumptions while preserving existing bridge evidence as migration input only.

founder_directives_recorded: The pipeline is universal and productized, not Oyatie-specific glue.
Do not add CLI, shell, or local bridge authority; canonical surfaces are cloud-native APIs, controllers, webhooks, services, and console/API operations.
GitHub Actions is an adapter and benchmark, not the north star.
Existing oya-* and cloud-* shapes are likely reorg targets and must not be extended as destination debt.
Benchmark best-in-class systems; take strengths, improve structural weaknesses, and track source repos as parity targets.
Rust is the first-party implementation language for owned control planes, reconcilers, policy evaluators, kernels, schedulers, and adapters.
Kubernetes and Linux userspace ABI compatibility are parity targets; internal kernel APIs are not stable contracts.
Contradictions become fixuptasks, not taste-based resolution.

GitHub Actions runner, ARC, toolkit, cache, checkout, runner-images, starter workflows
GitLab CI/CD and legacy plugin-controller CI
Neutral capability homes and current repo fit
Argo Workflows, CD, Rollouts, Events, Notifications, Image Updater
Kubernetes API machinery, controllers, watch/cache, admission, SSA, RBAC, scheduler, kubelet, conformance, Prow/SIG Release
Source tracking registry, golden fixtures, differential parity, replacement scoring
Kernel, OS, runtime reference stack and high-yield Rust replacement lanes
OS/runtime parity harness, conformance, differential testing, promotion gates

deprecated_destination_terms: oya-* component names as product-destination identifiers
cloud-* component names as product-destination identifiers
legacy plugin-controller CI as sole authority
shell workflow as canonical control plane
destination_naming_policy.allowed_legacy_use: Legacy oya-/cloud-prefixed paths may be referenced only as current-state inventory, bridge adapters, migration aliases, or evidence sources. New destination contracts, capability matrices, and promotion packets use shape-neutral names.
destination_naming_policy.adapter_rule: GitHub Actions, GitLab, legacy plugin-controller CI, Argo, Snyk, Trivy, driftctl, Prow, Kubernetes, OCI/runc/containerd, and Linux are benchmark/parity/adapter targets. None becomes the permanent product authority unless separately promoted by explicit governance.

strengths_to_adopt: broad vulnerability, misconfiguration, secret, license, SBOM, VEX, Kubernetes, filesystem, image, repo, VM, and IaC/drift coverage

reference_capability_matrix.native_shape: Rust ScannerAdapter, PrivateCollector, Finding, DriftObservation, SBOM, VEX, and EvidenceBundle APIs; no implicit code execution by default; all scan engines sandboxed and policy-declared.

strengths_to_adopt: stable userspace syscall ABI discipline
namespaces, cgroups, capabilities, seccomp, LSM, eBPF, procfs/sysfs/netlink compatibility
OCI/CRI interoperability and conformance
Firecracker-style Rust API, jailer/seccomp/cgroup hardening, minimal device model

node/worker isolation is frequently configured out-of-band

c-ward is experimental, incomplete, nightly-dependent, Linux GNU ABI-only today, and shells out to getent for user/DNS resolution, so it is a cautionary parity input rather than a production authority
reference_capability_matrix.native_shape: Rust runtime and sandbox control plane that preserves Linux userspace ABI, tests OCI/CRI/Kubernetes node compatibility, keeps libc/ABI compatibility behind explicit parity harnesses, and treats kernel-internal APIs plus experimental libc-replacement projects as implementation details until fresh conformance evidence exists.

resources.authority_boundary: All credentials are scoped, time-bound, and bound to tenant/run identities.

parity_target_source_tracking_contract.purpose: Make reference/source tracking executable without making external projects, adapters, or bridge CI systems authoritative.

c_ward_linux_libc_abi_rule.authority_boundary: c-ward is a pessimistic parity input for libc ABI experiments, never readiness or merge authority.

state_model.freshness_rule: Approved packets are terminal for reconciliation but CI, SLO, SBOM, rollback/DR, security, tenant, audit, and cost evidence expires on cadence and must refresh without reopening interviews unless authority/source changes.

principles: Map authoritative backlog first, then execute approved slices in isolated worktrees.
Maximize parallel evidence gathering and migration-safe prep; serialize promotion gates.
Prefer thin adapters and parity harnesses before deep replacement; replace highest-yield authority-bearing surfaces first.
Every slice defines success, failure, SLO objective, named failure modes, and a failure-injection test.

phases.name: Contradiction and authority reconciliation
phases.goal: Stop false product claims and stale naming debt from guiding implementation.
deliverables: Root pointer for this shape-neutral target exists.
Outdated legacy-plugin-controller-sole, GitHub-authority, oya-CLI, oya-*, and cloud-* destination assumptions are recorded as fixuptasks or superseded aliases.
Current-state rows classify each major productized-pipeline capability as tracked_inventory/fixuptask_required/promotion_pending, never product-ready by assertion.
verification: JSON parse validation for new/changed spec and current-state artifacts.
Fixuptask JSONL remains parseable and has no duplicate IDs for appended rows.

phases.name: API contract and resource-model slice
phases.goal: Create the neutral API/control-plane contract without new CLI or shell authority.
deliverables: OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/proto contracts for ChangeSet, PipelineSpec, RunPlan, WorkerLease, EvidenceBundle, ScannerRun, DriftObservation, ReleaseIntent, AdapterStatus, ParityTarget, PromotionPacket, and FixupTask.
Tenant isolation, audit-chain, policy-domain, status-condition, and freshness fields are required across resources.
Known-bad fixtures prove candidate bytes cannot rewrite gates, runners, status producers, or promotion policies.
verification: Contract schema validation.
Known-bad fixture suite for candidate-code-as-data, tenant isolation, and adapter non-authority.

phases.name: Parity registry and source-tracking harness
phases.goal: Religiously track reference repos/features without making them authority.
deliverables: ParityTarget rows for Kubernetes, Argo, GitHub Actions, GitLab, legacy plugin-controller CI, Snyk, Trivy, driftctl, Linux ABI, OCI/CRI, Firecracker, and c-ward-style Rust libc ABI experiments.
Feature rows include upstream version/ref, adopted behavior, rejected weakness, fixture path, differential test path, gap owner, and replacement score.
Freshness reaper marks source_changed_reopen_required when upstream sources change beyond accepted skew.
verification: Golden fixture parse tests.
I/O-free honest-claims validator rejects external authority, duplicate target IDs, missing pinned sources, and optimistic c-ward/kernel ABI claims.
Differential test scaffold proves at least one behavior per reference family is executable.

phases.name: Rust core kernels
phases.goal: Implement first-party kernels before adapters can claim authority.
deliverables: Pipeline graph resolver, admission evaluator, worker lease scheduler, evidence bundle builder, scanner finding model, drift observation model, release analysis model, parity scoring model.
No shell execution, local CLI, or vendor action is required for core state transitions.
All kernels are tenant-aware and policy-port driven.
verification: Unit/property tests for graph determinism, fail-closed policy, tenant partitioning, cache/artifact namespace separation, idempotency, and evidence immutability.
Failure-injection tests for stale evidence, missing tenant, adapter outage, scanner DB stale, worker lease expiry, and status producer spoofing.

phases.name: Adapter plane
phases.goal: Connect bridge systems without delegating product authority to them.
deliverables: GitHub adapter for webhook/status/artifact/cache translation.
GitLab/legacy-controller adapters for migration inventory only.
Argo adapters for workflow/CD/rollout parity where still used.
Snyk/Trivy/driftctl-compatible scanner/drift importers as data-plane collectors.
Kubernetes/OCI/Linux parity adapters for conformance and runtime proof.
verification: Adapter status cannot approve a PromotionPacket without first-party PolicyDecision and EvidenceBundle.
Tenant A cannot read/use tenant B repos, artifacts, caches, logs, secrets, statuses, deployments, rollback handles, or scanner results.

phases.name: Owned worker/runtime lanes
phases.goal: Incrementally replace bridge execution/runtime components by highest authority and risk yield.
deliverables: Hermetic worker lease executor behind API, initially using existing build/test substrates only as sandboxed execution engines.
Rust scanner collector, artifact/cache/evidence services, and sandbox controls.
Linux userspace ABI, OCI/CRI, and Kubernetes node parity harnesses before replacing runtime components.
verification: Conformance tests: Kubernetes API/controller subset, OCI/CRI, Linux ABI smoke/LTP subset, scanner fixtures, and Argo/GitHub/GitLab/legacy-controller import fixtures.
SLO/cost metrics: queue latency, run duration, cache hit ratio, scanner DB freshness, worker isolation denial, rollback RTO/RPO.

phases.name: Product readiness and hyperscaler promotion
phases.goal: Promote only evidence-backed, user-pain-reducing product slices.
deliverables: Dogfood journeys show real user pain reduction through the same public APIs tenants use.
Product-ready packets include user validation, API contracts, tenant isolation, audit, docs/console UX, supportability, and fresh CI evidence.
Hyperscaler-ready packets include tenant, audit, cost, SLO, security, SBOM, rollback/DR, and fresh CI proof.
verification: Promotion packet state machine enforcement.
Freshness expiry and revalidation cadence tests.

parallel_lanes.name: Serialized promotion gates
outputs: approved_product_ready or approved_hyperscaler_ready only when all evidence is current

success: No new destination artifact extends oya-* or cloud-* as canonical product shape.
No new local CLI/shell surface is used as authority.
Every pipeline decision is API/control-plane state backed by tenant, policy, evidence, audit, and freshness fields.
Adapters are explicitly non-authoritative and deletion/parity criteria exist.
Reference parity rows track upstream source versions/refs and executable fixtures.
Promotion packets cannot be approved without current tenant, audit, cost, SLO, security, SBOM, rollback/DR, and CI evidence.
failure_modes: Vendor status, GitHub action, legacy plugin-controller CI job, Argo CRD, Snyk/Trivy CLI, driftctl output, or local shell becomes direct promotion authority.
Candidate PR bytes can modify their own gate definitions/status producer/runner isolation.
Tenant pipelines share credentials, cache namespace, artifact namespace, logs/evidence, release ledger, or rollback handles.
Scan engines execute untrusted package/build tools without explicit sandbox policy.
Linux internal kernel API is treated as stable product ABI.
Kubernetes/Argo/GitHub/GitLab/legacy-controller feature parity is asserted without source/ref-tracked tests.
Approved promotion evidence expires but packet remains presented as fresh.

slo_objectives.name: admission_decision_latency
slo_objectives.target: p95 <= 1s for policy + graph admission on normal PR-sized ChangeSet; overload returns explicit backpressure not silent pass

slo_objectives.name: evidence_freshness
slo_objectives.target: 0 approved promotions with expired CI/SLO/SBOM/DR/security/cost/tenant/audit evidence

slo_objectives.name: adapter_non_authority
slo_objectives.target: 0 paths where adapter status alone can produce approved_product_ready or approved_hyperscaler_ready

failure_injection_tests: Candidate PR edits gate definition to skip tests: admission rejects from trusted trunk/controller diff.
Tenant A reuses tenant B cache key/artifact/log path: policy denies and evidence records violation.
GitHub status green but first-party EvidenceBundle missing SBOM: promotion remains fixuptask_required.
Scanner input package requests install/build script: sandbox blocks by default unless explicit policy permits.
Upstream Kubernetes fixture behavior changes: ParityTarget becomes source_changed_reopen_required.
Linux ABI differential test mismatch: runtime replacement lane blocks promotion.
